```{r}
#| include = FALSE
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"

```

```{r}
#| label = "setup",
#| echo = FALSE,
#| message = FALSE
library(rpkgkit)
dir <- tempdir()
usethis::create_package(path = dir, open = FALSE)
```

# Create package infrastructure

## A startup message

`use_zzz()` creates a package documentation file with `.onLoad`, `.onAttach`,
and `%||%`. It is similar to `usethis::use_package_doc()` while also providing
a useful starting template.

```{r}
#| label = "use_zzz"
use_zzz(path = dir, open = FALSE)
```

## Check missing function in `_pkgdown` reference

`check_pkgdown_reference()` identifies exported functions that are absent from
the `reference` section of `_pkgdown.yml`.

```{r}
#| label = "check_pkgdown_reference",
#| eval = FALSE
check_pkgdown_reference(pkg = dir)
```

## Configure the clangd language server

`use_clangd()` writes a `.clangd` configuration file that lets the clangd
language server find the system R headers and the `include/` directory of the
packages you pass in `include` (`Rcpp`, `RcppEigen` and `RcppArmadillo` by
default). Packages that are not installed are skipped with a warning.

```{r}
#| label = "use_clangd"
use_clangd(path = dir, overwrite = TRUE)
```

When `path` is a package root, the file also disables background indexing for
the `R/` directory (which holds no C++ code) and adds `.clangd` to
`.Rbuildignore`.

```{r}
#| label = "use_clangd_include",
#| eval = FALSE
use_clangd(path = dir, include = c("Rcpp", "BH"), overwrite = TRUE)
```

# Vendor permissively licensed code

`use_vendor()` records attribution and licensing information when incorporating
selected source files from a permissively licensed GitHub R package. It creates
an `inst/vendor/` directory, a `R/vendor-*.R` file, and updates relevant
`DESCRIPTION` fields.

```{r}
#| label = "use_vendor"
try(use_vendor(
  pkg = "WangLabCSU/rpkgkit",
  "43_use_vendor.R",
  branch = "main",
  path = dir
))
```

Only packages with a supported permissive license can be vendored. Review the
acknowledgement text printed by the function and add it to your README when
appropriate.

# `usethis` extensions

Use the following helpers from the package root:

## Use R 4.1.0 version

R 4.1.0 introduced the pipe (`|>`) and anonymous function `\()`. If these syntaxes need to be used in a package, the R package must require at least R version 4.1.0.

```{r}
#| label = "use_r_v4.1.0"
use_r_v4.1.0(path = dir)
```

## Add URL in `DESCRIPTION`

```{r}
#| label = "use_url",
#| eval = FALSE
use_url(dir)
```

## Add bug reports URL in `DESCRIPTION`

```{r}
#| label = "use_bugreports",
#| eval = FALSE
use_bugreports(dir)
```

# Open CFF

CITATION.cff files are plain text files with human- and machine-readable citation information for software and datasets.

Code developers can include such files in their source code repositories to let others know how to correctly cite their software.

```{r}
#| label = "use_cff",
#| eval = FALSE
open_cffinit()
```

**This cannot replace `usethis::use_citation()`**, it just complements project.


# Global ignore-file templates

Use `add_global_rbuildignore()` and `add_global_gitgnore()` to add the
corresponding global ignore-file templates to a package.

```{r}
#| label = "add_global_rbuildignore"
add_global_rbuildignore(path = dir)
```

```{r}
#| label = "add_global_gitgnore"
add_global_gitgnore(pkg = dir)
```

# Check system dependencies

Some packages need system development libraries (graphics and font libraries,
for example) to compile. `check_sysdeps()` detects the package manager in use
(`dpkg`, `rpm`, `pacman`, `apk` or `brew`), checks each dependency with it, and
reports every hit and miss together with a ready-to-paste install command for
the missing ones.

```{r}
#| label = "check_sysdeps",
#| eval = FALSE
check_sysdeps()
```

With `deps = NULL` (the default), a built-in list of graphics and font libraries
(`freetype`, `libjpeg`, `libpng`, `libtiff`, `libwebp`, `harfbuzz`, `fribidi`,
`fontconfig`) is checked using the names that the detected package manager
expects. Pass your own names in `deps`, and optionally set `manager` to check
against a manager other than the detected one:

```{r}
#| label = "check_sysdeps_deps",
#| eval = FALSE
check_sysdeps(c("freetype-devel", "libwebp-devel"), manager = "rpm")
```

The result is returned invisibly as a named logical vector, so it can be reused
in scripts. Set `verbose = FALSE` to keep the run silent:

```{r}
#| label = "check_sysdeps_result",
#| eval = FALSE
ok <- check_sysdeps(verbose = FALSE)
ok[!ok]
```

# Detect the Positron version

`get_positron_version()` reports the version of the Positron IDE that hosts the
current R session. It is useful for diagnostics, bug reports, or for enabling
IDE-specific behaviour only on recent builds.

```{r}
#| label = "get_positron_version",
#| eval = FALSE
get_positron_version() # e.g. "2025.01.0"
get_positron_version(long = TRUE) # e.g. "2025.01.0-123"
```

The version is looked up in three steps, in this order:

1. the `POSITRON_VERSION` environment variable set by Positron for its R
   sessions (`POSITRON_LONG_VERSION`, which also carries the build number, when
   `long = TRUE`);
2. the `.ps.positron_version()` helper that the IDE injects into the session;
3. the `positron --version` command-line tool.

If the session does not run inside Positron and no `positron` executable is on
`PATH`, the function returns `NA_character_` instead of throwing an error, so it
is safe to call in any session, including CI.
